text:
Sam: quick FYI — noticed a spike of 429s from requests hitting private endpoints where the X-Workspace-ID header was missing. Gateway fell back to hosted pool and we ended up mixing traffic. not great :grimacing:
Priya: ugh. any sample request or trace id?
Sam: pasted one from logs:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.internal
X-Private-Endpoint: true
Authorization: Bearer ****
Content-Type: application/json
Body: { prompt: \"hello\" }
```
(no X-Workspace-ID)
Jordan: is the gateway currently treating missing workspace header as \"public\" and routing to shared-hosted? that sounds like the configuration we had months ago. :thinking:
Li: yeah, that’s the current fallback — if no workspace header, route by auth token -> hosted catalog. for private endpoints we used to require workspace scoping but there was a regression in the header enforcement rule set.
Marta: two concerns: 1) data isolation risk for private endpoints, 2) quota/usage attribution — we might bill a workspace incorrectly. both are bad.
Priya: proposal: if X-Private-Endpoint:true AND no X-Workspace-ID, gateway should:
  1) route to an \"isolation-hold\" dedicated pool (low-capacity, throttled)
  2) emit telemetry event routing.decision=\"hold_for_identity\" reason=\"missing_workspace_header\"
  3) surface in console as a flagged request with ability to approve/assign workspace
works?
Jordan: I like the safety-first approach. avoids accidental cross-tenant execution. how disruptive is adding an extra pool?
Li: we can implement the pool as a logical fallback that maps to existing dedicated capacity with strict qps and zero-cache policy. cost delta minimal. main work: routing rule + telemetry + console UX.
ops-bot: detected 12 requests in last 6h matching the pattern (private endpoint + missing workspace header). added tag \"missing_workspace_header\" to traces.
Sam: thanks — we should also include a short-lived quota bump flow so user can request routing to hosted if desired (with manual approval). otherwise default to hold.
Marta: console UX: add a per-request \"routing trace\" column in Debug -> Recent Requests, show policy_version, decision_reason, matched_rules, and a CTA \"assign workspace\" that opens a small modal to attach workspace ID and reprocess.
Priya: for telemetry namespacing I suggest: routing.policy_version, routing.decision, routing.matched_clause, routing.fallback_pool, tenant.attribution_hint (if any). keep keys stable so billing can consume.
Jordan: small implementation plan:
  - gateway rule change + unit tests (canary 5% for 24h)
  - telemetry event + new tags (add to bigquery schema)
  - console flag + modal (feature flag behind rollout)
  - ops playbook update
deploy-bot: canary job queued. canary target: gateway-prod, 5% of private-endpoint traffic, 24h window.
Li: one API edge case: what about requests with workspace header present but auth token belongs to a different workspace? we should still validate token -> workspace mapping and decline/hold if mismatch.
Sam: agreed — add validation step: if X-Workspace-ID present, verify token maps or else hold and emit reason=\"workspace_token_mismatch\".
Marta: quick question — do we need a remediation API to retroactively reassign held requests after customer provides mapping? Reactivating logs?
Priya: yes, console action should kick off a reprocess job that replays the request into the selected pool (idempotent replay) and logs an audit entry.
Jordan: timeline: devs can spike gateway rule + telemetry in 2 days, console modal in 5 days, canary next week.
Sam: sounds good. I'll open a short RFC with the rule DSL change and telemetry examples. cc @Marta @Li for console and billing impacts. :thumbsup:
Marta: :eyes: please include sample console screenshots in RFC mockups.
ops-bot: noted. ticket created: PLAT-4982 \"gateway: default hold for missing workspace header on private endpoints\"
deploy-bot: will follow up with canary results in #eng-platform after rollout.
Sam: thanks everyone — feel better having a safe default.
